What I didn't get under budget is speed: the new "what still holds together" check per blow takes about 8 ms headless (median) and 17 ms in the browser, against a target of 5 ms or less.

**Why it dragged as one:** when the cut went through, the code only split the log in its wood bookkeeping, into two stretches on the same tree object. Physically it stayed one body, and dragging moves that body. The split was also decided by a fixed rule: a section with 35% of its wood left counted as "cut through". So a visible third of the log still joined the halves while the bookkeeping already treated them as two (repro: pine D20 on glade, 44 swings, split at 34.9% left, one body).

**What I changed**
- **Wood connectivity** (`world/chop/wood_cuts.gd`): after every blow, the cut area is checked cell by cell for which pieces of wood still touch. A fast path handles the common case. Bits left hanging in the air come off:
  - under 30 cm³ (a chip-sized splinter, about 20 g) they go as chips of exactly their volume;
  - larger ones become a loose piece of exactly their volume (an item if under 10 kg, else a timber).

  They are also removed from the picture, so what you see and what the model holds agree.
- **When the two halves part:** either no wood joins them any more, or the bridge can't carry the lighter half. The bridge rule treats the lighter half as hanging off it by its own weight times half its length. It uses the same green-wood strength the tree fall uses. In practice a D20 pine log tore with 13–27% of the section left, after 11–30 swings.
- **Two bodies** (`systems/build_system.gd`): the tree keeps the crown side; the butt side becomes a Timber carrying exactly its cut cells. That timber can be dragged, chopped and built from like any loose timber.
- **The new timber starts safely:**
  - it ignores what it was spawned inside (the stump, the log) until it no longer touches it;
  - it is lifted onto the real ground surface;
  - if there is no ground collider under it at all, it lies still where the log lay.
- **Same rule everywhere a cut happens:** built rods and loose timbers (`world/build/piece_breaker.gd`, `world/build/rod.gd`) and branches (`world/chop/branches.gd`). Upright posts still part at 3% left, as before.

- **Dragging** (`systems/carry_system.gd`): skips the split log's old colliders until it redraws. Before this, a valley drag used a 14 m log length.

## time per blow (min of 3 runs: the hub is loaded). godot --headless --path . -s <this> [-- R=0.1]

func _wedge(dir: Vector2, h: float, depth: float, R: float, open: float, half_w: float) -> PackedFloat64Array:
	# a V trough across the log: its floor line `depth` in from the bark at `dir`, faces opening `open`
	# (slope per metre outward) either side of h, as wide as half_w across
	var u := Vector3(dir.x, 0.0, dir.y).normalized()
	var apex := R - depth                      # distance of the V floor from the axis along u
	var ps: Array = []
	# below the upper face: y - h <= open * (u.p - apex)  ->  y - open*u.p <= h - open*apex
	ps.append(Plane(Vector3(-open * u.x, 1.0, -open * u.z).normalized(), (h - open * apex) / Vector3(-open * u.x, 1.0, -open * u.z).length()))
	ps.append(Plane(Vector3(-open * u.x, -1.0, -open * u.z).normalized(), (-h - open * apex) / Vector3(-open * u.x, -1.0, -open * u.z).length()))
	ps.append(Plane(-u, -(apex - 0.001)))       # u.p >= apex
	ps.append(Plane(u, R + 0.05))
	var side := Vector3(-u.z, 0.0, u.x)
	ps.append(Plane(side, half_w))
	ps.append(Plane(-side, half_w))
	return WoodCuts.pack(ps)

	pq = Geometry3D.get_closest_points_between_segments(eye, eye - n * (0.7 * float(sw.haft)), cap[0], cap[1])
	return pq[0].distance_to(pq[1]) > rad + 0.005 + slack


'''

The crosshair only turns the plane of the swing. Something nearer than the circle is met by the haft or cheeks first. Something beyond it is out of reach.\n   - The marker still shows only where the circle really touches.\n   - When the crosshair is on something out of reach, a grey dot and the word «далеко» appear there.\n   - When the haft meets the wood before the blade, a red «близко» appears next to the red jam mark.\n   - The bots now stand at the exact distance where the circle passes 4 cm into what they look at. The one-hand axe reaches the ground only crouched.\n\n2. Ready pose. Before the wind-up, a swung tool is now held at the side the blow will come from:\n   - from the right: the head at the right, blade toward the middle;\n   - overhead: raised up-right, edge down;\n   - from the left: across the body;\n   - from below: low at the hands' side, edge up.\n   - The left hand and one-hand grips are mirrored.\n   - The pose turns smoothly with the wheel (eased), and the wind-up and recovery start from it.\n   - My first version placed the axe on its real arc. **Fixed**
1. **Hole in the glade ground (root cause found).** The integrator saw no ground collider under a felled log's butt. A new dug patch (litter, or a log pressed in) waits for its collider to be built. Meanwhile, any other patch opening in the same collision chunk rebuilt the ground without the waiting patch's cells, which left a hole. In tests the hole lasted the whole run. Fix: new `DigView.collides(key)`; `Glade._dig_col` and `ValleyMap._col_cells` now cut holes only under patches that already have their own collider. The `LOG_SPLIT_RAY` "no ground" lines are gone on the glade.
2. **Nothing hangs after a log is cut through.** I rewrote `BuildSystem._drop_hanging_end`:
   - It samples the underside at 17 points against the ground and static bodies (stumps, rocks, built pieces, frozen logs).
   - If nothing bears, the log drops straight. Otherwise it turns about the bearing point nearest the cut end, but only when the log's weight (crown branches included) lies past that point.
   - On every peer the final pose is set at once inside the event; the fall is only animated on screen. The next blow on the log finishes it, and a drag takes over.
   - Valley: the cut end hung 0.26 m, and the log turns 1.2° about a point 6.36 m in. The integrator's turn about the far end would have pushed that middle point into the ground.
3. **Branch stopped mid-tip on a log.** The grass hold in `Timber._on_grass` now applies only when a contact is the ground, not another log or a stone. I added a settle-bot case `tip`. With the old rule it fails (far end 0.193 m in the air); with the new one it passes (0.017 m). Settle has 0 fails on both maps.
4. **Wall-stone preview promised a stone that never came.** The integrator blamed the push energy, but the real cause is size: the 0.13 L flake is below `MIN_CHUNK` (0.5 L), so it flies off as chips.
